title.narrative: NIHR Development Awards Call 1: Population-based heart failure feasibility study in Maputo, Mozambique

description.narrative:
A low-and-middle-income country (LMIC) award led by Universidade Eduardo Mondlane, Mozambique in partnership with the University of Glasgow, United Kingdom which aims to generate preliminary data on causes of heart failure in the Mozambican population, and demonstrate approaches to population-based studies within low-resourced African settings.
Pre-existing data suggests that heart failure in Africa varies from the rest of the world due to a prevalence within a younger age demographic. Additionally, there are different causes and risk factors for heart failure in the African context, which is limited to data collected from hospital patients and not inclusive of cases not managed in hospitals. To implement measures that can be effective in preventing and controlling heart failure, it is important to know exactly how it presents at the population level. As such, data generated via award activity will guide the design and implementation aimed at bridging the knowledge gap of data more representative of the country’s population.
Commencing in January 2025, the twelve-month award will engage with community leaders and local authorities before undertaking data collection across a rural and urban setting within Mozambique. As a result, the design and implementation process of this study will employ community engagement and involvement to ensure integration of community perspectives and experiences, and increased collaboration between teams at the University of Glasgow in the United Kingdom and Maputo Central Hospital in Mozambique will bolster capacity strengthening initiatives.

The award has eight objectives: 1. To demonstrate the feasibility of conducting a population-based study in a low resourced African setting and obtain preliminary data on the prevalence, aetiology and risk factors of heart failure in Mozambique. 2. To design and apply questionnaires to estimate the proportion of eligible people who are willing to participate, the proportion of participants who drop out and the standard deviation that will be used for the sample size calculation in the follow-up study on a representative urban and rural population sample of Mozambique. 3. To pilot-test study tools/questionnaires and measurement procedures for assessment of prevalence, risk factors and the diagnosis of heart failure. To describe the process for conducting population-based heart failure research in a low resourced African setting, including the challenges found and actions taken to overcome them. 4. To describe the process for conducting a population-based heart failure research in a low resourced African setting, including the challenges found and actions taken to overcome them during planning, patient recruitment and collection of epidemiological, clinical and biospecimen data. 5. To determine and compare the age and sex-specific prevalence of heart failure via questionnaire in a sample of both the urban and rural population of Mozambique. 6. To describe the antecedents (risk factors and aetiologies) and specific phenotypes of heart failure found in a sample of the population of Mozambique, according to residence in urban or rural area and socio-economic status. 7. To measure household expenditure, according to residence in urban or rural areas. 8. To evaluate the quality of life of participants, including heart failure patients, according to residence in urban or rural areas.
